newsitem.title: GERMANY: VAW chairman sees 1997 aluminium use steady or up.
newsitem.headline: VAW chairman sees 1997 aluminium use steady or up.

text.p: Jochen Schirner, chairman of German aluminium producer VAW aluminium AG, said on Tuesday aluminium demand in 1997 may stabilise or grow as consumers replenish stocks.
Schirner spoke at the annual news conference of metals industry association WVM, where he is president, and stressed his remark applied to the entire sector, not just VAW.
"Demand in Europe is developing favourably and in addition, processors and end users' stocks appear to be empty," he said. He did not give a consumption forecast.
Primary aluminium output in Germany, which accounts for one third of the European total, in 1996 was unchanged from 1996 at 576,000 tonnes, WVM data showed.
Secondary aluminium output in 1996 amounted to 416,000 tonnes, which was also broadly steady.
VAW, part of utility group VIAG AG, permanently removed 30,000 tonnes a year of capacity from the market in 1995.
Germany in 1996 imported 1,066,000 tonnes of aluminium, 19 percent less than in 1995, not counting semi-fabricated products. It exported 250,000 tonnes, 4.9 percent less than a year earlier.

Schirner said supply additions from Russian exports were under control as Russia had been integrated into the group of world producers and would not be able to export more than two million tonnes a year in future.
